user_feedback: Unblurred comparison reveals stuttering, worse in Mux than Beeper.

original_source_observations.interpretation: The stutter is not solely an editing artifact. These are recording measurements, not proof of app-rendering frame times.

export_cause.problem: All filter stages and the output were forced to 30 fps, discarding real motion updates from nominal-60-Hz captures.
export_cause.measurement_method: Compare consecutive 80 x 174 grayscale frames in matching gesture windows; count mean absolute luma differences greater than 0.8. Counts depend on that threshold and window boundaries, and are not app-display FPS measurements.
export_cause.fix: One 60-fps constant drives scene budgets, resampling, concatenation, frame-background input and output encoding. Source ranges, layout and action speed remain unchanged.
export_cause.limits: No interpolation or optical flow. Seven of eight sampled gesture windows retained all counted source updates; one Mux window counted 9 rather than 10. The original 183.3-ms source pause still appears at 183.3 ms in the new export. Smooth scrolling is not claimed.

capture_instrumentation.matched_live_workflow: Inbox scroll, approved family conversation, thread scroll, edge-back to inbox. Recorded live as Argent fragments.
capture_instrumentation.interpretation: Both diagnostic takes wrote every received frame. Gaps exist before the recorder callback; the Mac writer is not shown to be their cause. Entire command intervals include idle time, so those maxima must not be presented as matched gesture or app-frame benchmarks. Run-to-run differences prevent assigning blame to Mux from these recordings alone.
capture_instrumentation.cleanup: Stopped only the physical iPhone's Argent runner; no sends, reactions or deletions. Existing app sign-ins and unrelated app edits were left intact.

new_local_preview.visual_check: Full-resolution inbox frame inspected; native status chrome and inbox content remain visible, with no replacement header or misleading privacy caption.

verification.command: uv run python -m unittest discover -s demo -p 'test_*.py' -v
verification.red_before_fix: A real FFmpeg fixture alternating black and white at 60 Hz produced only 30 output frames instead of 60.
verification.green_after_fix: Masked and explicitly unredacted exports each preserve all 60 fixture frames and all 59 alternating transitions.
verification.privacy_default: Masks remain enabled by default. --unredacted is explicit, and the frame generator has a matching explicit option.
verification.avfoundation_metadata_correction: nominalFrameRate returned 30.000002 for the exact 30-fps legacy export. The verifier now derives FPS from the rational minimum frame duration, retaining strict 30/60-fps validation and exact expected frame counts.
verification.warnings: Standalone Swift helpers still emit known macOS 27 AVFoundation deprecation warnings; builds and runtime checks pass. No app or framework build was needed.

still_open: Does normal finger scrolling on the phone stutter without automation or capture? Asked the user; answer pending.
If manual scrolling is smooth, isolate automation versus wired-screen transport with a manual baseline.
If Mux itself stutters without capture, profile its scroll/render path before modifying app or framework code.
Do not treat a 60-fps stream label, zero reported writer drops, or a contact sheet as proof of smooth motion.
